title: PSwarm: A hybrid solver for linearly constrained global derivative-free optimization
contribution: Extends the PSwarm hybrid (particle swarm in the search step, coordinate/tangent-cone polling) from bounds to general linear inequality constraints, with a feasible maximum-volume-ellipsoid initial swarm, ratio-test-damped particle moves, and ε-active tangent-cone polling. It is benchmarked on a 110+10-problem AMPL collection with a new 'function profile'. The paper contains no convergence theorem.
problem_entry: Global DFO practice relies on heuristics with little benchmarking (p. 2), and the bound-constrained PSwarm could not handle general, often unrelaxable, linear constraints (pp. 5, 18).
key_idea: Keep PSO as the search step and coordinate-type polling around the best particle. Make the swarm feasible (MVE initialisation, per-component and per-constraint ratio tests) and poll along positive generators of the ε-active tangent cone with ε = O(α), falling back to D⊕ (pp. 6–11).
assumptions: Linear inequalities only (unrelaxable, so a feasible method is used); f possibly nonsmooth or noisy; MVE needs a bounded region, full-rank A and a strictly feasible point. No convergence theory: mesh projection omitted, sufficient decrease ignored, and a D⊕ fallback in the degenerate case (pp. 3, 7, 8, 10–11).
proof_devices: none (no lemmas or theorems in the paper, checked pp. 1–22)
constructive: tangent-cone generators D = [B −B N −N] from a QR of C̄ᵀ, with ε halved until C̄ has full row rank (Algorithm 3.2, p. 11)
constructive: ratio-test step lengths keeping particles feasible (eqs. 8–9, p. 9)
experiments: 110 linearly constrained AMPL problems (from 1564) and 10 random-constraint nonconvex problems; baselines ASA, NOMADm, DIRECT; 10 runs per stochastic solver; performance profiles of min/avg/max final value at 2000/10000 evaluations; function profiles (evaluations to relative error τ = 0.1); no initial guesses for fairness (pp. 11–18, 20).
positioning: Criticises heuristic-only global DFO practice; builds on Vaz & Vicente 2007; adopts Kolda–Lewis–Torczon's ε = O(α) without their sufficient decrease; simplifies NOMADm's degeneracy handling; rejects data profiles for stated reasons (pp. 2, 10, 13, 17).
writing: The algorithm box marks in bold what changed from the prior version; contributions come in three layers (extension, benchmark collection, function profiles); candid about process ('intensive testing') and doubt on nonlinear constraints (pp. 6, 18–20).
limits_future: Nonlinear constraints are open and a penalty/augmented-Lagrangian route 'might not be the way to proceed'; the degenerate fallback is not covered by theory; no guarantee is stated for the linear-constraint version (pp. 10–11, 20).

title: Incorporating minimum Frobenius norm models in direct search
contribution: Adds to SID-PSM's coordinate-search skeleton a search step that minimises minimum-Frobenius-norm (or regression) quadratic models built from all previously evaluated points in a step-size-tied trust region. Data profiles show clear gains over other direct-search codes, and wins over NEWUOA on noisy or nonsmooth problems at larger budgets.
problem_entry: Moré–Wild benchmarks showed model-based trust-region codes beating direct search even on piecewise-smooth and noisy problems, so the paper combines the two (p. 2).
key_idea: Keep search/poll direct search; build MFN models (regression above (n+1)(n+2)/2 points) from store-all points, 80% nearest and 20% farthest, with deliberately loose geometry, and minimise them in Δ_k = σ_k α_{k−1} max‖d‖; opportunistic poll on [e −e I −I] ordered by simplex gradient (pp. 6–9).
assumptions: Recalled fully-linear error bounds assume a Lipschitz gradient and Λ-poisedness (pp. 4–5), but the algorithm does not enforce poisedness (p. 8); simple-decrease acceptance (p. 6); no convergence result is stated; unconstrained only (p. 6).
proof_devices: design justification: gradient-error constant C_pΛ_L[C_f + ‖H‖] grows with ‖H‖, so minimise ‖H‖_F (Thm 2.1, p. 4)
combination of Thm 2.1 and the MFN Hessian bound (Thm 2.2) gives fully-linear MFN models (p. 5)
experiments: Moré–Wild data profiles, 53 problems × 4 classes (smooth, nonstochastic noisy, piecewise smooth, stochastic noisy), n ∈ [2, 12], τ = 1e−3 and 1e−7, 1500 evaluations in units of n+1; baselines NEWUOA, NMSMAX, APPSPACK; NEWUOA best on smooth problems (pp. 9–10).
positioning: Model-based codes (DFO, NEWUOA, MNH) as the efficiency benchmark; Powell's least-updating MFN tested and found worse in this context; loose geometry justified via Fasano–Morales–Nocedal; builds on SID-PSM; first-attempt claim ('to our knowledge') (pp. 2, 5, 8, 15).
writing: Design-by-elimination narrative ('report the various possibilities and describe the ones which we found to be the most successful'); negative result against NEWUOA stated in the introduction; frequent hedges (pp. 2, 7, 8).
limits_future: Below NEWUOA on smooth problems with small budgets; the constrained MFN search step is future research; no convergence statement for the modified method (pp. 2, 10, 15).

title: Direct multisearch for multiobjective optimization
contribution: Introduces direct multisearch (DMS): directional direct search generalised to multiobjective DFO without aggregation, by iterating on a list of nondominated (x; α) pairs with success defined as a change in the list. It proves that some limit point is Pareto–Clarke stationary (lattice or sufficient-decrease globalisation) and releases a 100-problem AMPL MOO collection with MOO performance and data profiles.
problem_entry: Black-box or noisy multiobjective problems; a-priori aggregation needs weights and yields one point, and weight sweeps or normal-boundary intersection have known drawbacks (pp. 1–2).
key_idea: Replace the incumbent with a filtered list of nondominated points; success = list change; sufficient decrease = outside the ℓ∞ ρ̄-neighbourhood of the dominated region; search, poll and step update unchanged; reduces to direct search when m = 1 (pp. 2, 4–7).
assumptions: Compact union of level sets, F bounded (Assumption 4.1, p. 9); F Lipschitz near x*; refining directions dense in the Clarke tangent cone (stronger than a dense D, p. 13); lattice route A.1–A.4 or sufficient-decrease route A.5 (pp. 28–30); numerics use a non-dense D⊕ with ρ̄ = 0 (p. 20).
proof_devices: lattice route: finite lattice ∩ compact set plus no-cycling by transitivity of dominance means finitely many successes (Thm A.1, p. 30)
sufficient-decrease route: hypercube packing in objective space; each success removes a ρ*-hypercube from the nondominated region (Thm A.2, pp. 30–31)
Clarke–Jahn lim sup along a refining subsequence with ρ̄(α_k‖d_k‖) added and subtracted, then pigeonhole over the m objectives to fix j(d) (Thm 4.8, p. 13)
density of refining directions gives Pareto–Clarke criticality (Thm 4.9, p. 14); sanity corollaries for m = 1 and for an eventually singleton list (Cors 4.10–4.11, p. 14)
experiments: 100 bound-constrained AMPL MOO problems (69 bi-, 30 tri-, 1 four-objective per Table 5.1), public; 8 solvers, best 3 reported (AMOSA, BIMADS, NSGA-II); pairwise purity, spread Γ/Δ, MOO data profiles; 10 runs for stochastic solvers (best/worst); 20000-evaluation budget; DMS initialisation ablation; cache and spread-based poll-centre improvement (pp. 15–25).
positioning: A-posteriori class, against weighted sums and NBI; generalises GPS, GSS and MADS; nonsmooth analysis follows Audet–Dennis; neutral data-driven comparison with evolutionary codes and BIMADS (pp. 2, 11–12, 22–25, 30).
writing: Coined name justified by the m = 1 reduction; abstract states the gap between the weak theorem and the 'impressive' practice; test set and profiles framed as by-products; worked example before theory; intuition in the text, rigour in the appendix (pp. 1–2, 7–10, 26).
limits_future: Only a stationary limit point of the front is guaranteed; the density assumption is strong and not met by the tested poll; future: swarm or model search steps, simplex-gradient polls, parallel polling, preference insertion, discontinuous extension (pp. 13, 20, 26–28).

title: Analysis of direct searches for discontinuous functions
contribution: Extends the refining-direction stationarity theory of directional direct search (MADS and sufficient-decrease/GSS variants) from Lipschitz to lower-semicontinuous, directionally Lipschitz functions via Rockafellar's upper subderivative (rebuilt for constraints). It shows that, for two-piece step discontinuities, the method approaches the limit along the better piece. 2-D numerics are designed around the hypotheses.
problem_entry: Audet–Dennis stationarity needs f Lipschitz near the limit point, little is known for discontinuous f, and applications (Omega ratio, parameter tuning, error analysis, aircraft design) are discontinuous (pp. 2–4).
key_idea: Same generic algorithm with the forcing function on the displacement ρ̄(α_k‖d_k‖) (making lattice and sufficient decrease compatible); replace the Clarke derivative by f↑ = f⁺ = f°_R on the directionally Lipschitz cone; prove best-branch identification by Lipschitz extension across a step boundary (pp. 4, 6, 11–17).
assumptions: Bounded level set; f lsc at x*; directionally Lipschitz with respect to the refining direction; lim f(x_k) = f(x*) assumed in §3; dense refining directions (in a ball, or for every subsequence); §4 needs a finite partition with nonempty interiors, the exterior-cone property and Lipschitz pieces, and exactly two pieces for the strong result (pp. 7, 9, 11–17).
proof_devices: Audet–Dennis lim sup along a refining subsequence with base points x_k →_f x*, with ρ̄(α_k‖d_k‖) added and subtracted (Thm 3.1, pp. 11–12)

constrained extension of Rockafellar: epi f↑(x; ·) = tangent cone of the restricted epigraph; directional Lipschitzness ⇔ hypertangency in the epigraph; f↑ = f⁺ = f°_R on D_{f,Ω} (Prop. A.1, Thms A.1–A.2, pp. 25–29)
lim-inf representation of f↑ on the tangent cone (eq. 9, p. 28; Thm 3.2, p. 13)

proof by extension: Lipschitz continuous extension (constant 3L+2) and a McShane extension strictly decreasing into an exterior cone give a contradiction forcing infinitely many poll points out of the piece (Props 4.1–4.2, Thm 4.1, pp. 14–17)
two pieces: monotone f(x_k) plus lsc give f(x_k) → f(x*) along the better piece (Cor. 4.1, p. 17)
experiments: Four 2-D lsc functions each meeting or violating a named hypothesis (two-piece gap, non-Lipschitz continuous, empty-interior piece, four pieces); NOMADm LTMADS vs a sufficient-decrease variant ([Q −Q], ρ(t) = t²); 10 runs, then a 100-start grid × 10 runs at tolerances 1e−7 and 1e−10; failures only where hypotheses fail (pp. 17–23).
positioning: Continues the Audet–Dennis Clarke-calculus line for GPS and MADS; generalises Rockafellar 1980 to constraints and notes differing hypertangency definitions; claims a first nonsmooth GSS analysis as a by-product (pp. 3, 5, 11).
writing: Hypothesis-precise abstract; explicit reader guidance and geometric intuition for f↑; modest final remarks with a mechanistic explanation of the two-piece barrier; numerics framed as agreeing with theory (pp. 1, 10–11, 22–23).
limits_future: Only two pieces (poll points may approach the border more slowly than the iterates); lim f(x_k) = f(x*) assumed in §3; 2-D numerics only; SKILL.md records a 2024 counterexample to the result, whose target step was not determined from this text (pp. 11, 17–23).

The problem in extending this result to more than two local steps or branches lies on the fact that the speed at which the poll points approach the border of a step domain can be slower than the speed at which these points approach the iterates.
